sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐秘。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: I fell in love with architecture in Chicago, a city known for its pioneering, stunning skyscrapers.
sentences.zh: 我是在芝加哥爱上建筑的，这座城市以其开创性且惊艳的摩天大楼而闻名。

sentences.en: Every good thing you hear about Chicago architecture is true.
sentences.zh: 你听到的关于芝加哥建筑的所有好话都是真的。

sentences.en: And whenever anyone I know takes a trip to Chicago, I tell them,
sentences.zh: 每当我认识的人去芝加哥旅行时，我都会告诉他们，

sentences.en: the one thing that you have to do is go on the Chicago Architecture Foundation Center boat tour.
sentences.zh: 有一件事你绝对不能错过，那就是去参加芝加哥建筑基金会中心的乘船游览。

sentences.en: From the river, you can take in all these amazing buildings, while a whip-smart, passionate docent tells you story after story of grand ambitions and visionary architects.
sentences.zh: 从河面上，你可以饱览所有这些惊艳的建筑，同时一位机智、热情的讲解员会为你讲述一个又一个关于宏大抱负和远见卓识的建筑师的故事。

sentences.en: But it's important to note that only a small percentage of structures are designed by architects.
sentences.zh: 但需要指出的是，只有极小比例的结构是由建筑师设计的。

sentences.en: And while an iconic building along the skyline might be the best way to identify a city at a distance,
sentences.zh: 虽然天际线旁标志性的建筑可能是从远处辨认一座城市的最佳方式，

sentences.en: up close, it's the subtle cues and vernacular design.
sentences.zh: 但在近处，则是那些微妙的线索和本土设计，

sentences.en: that make the city what it is.
sentences.zh: 造就了这座城市的本色。

sentences.en: If someone were to blindfold me, spin me around, and drop me in one of Chicago's 1,900 miles worth of alleyways,
sentences.zh: 如果有人蒙上我的眼睛，把我转晕，然后把我扔进芝加哥长达1900英里的某条小巷里，

sentences.en: I would know what city I was in instantly.
sentences.zh: 我能立刻认出这是哪座城市。

sentences.en: Not because I could see the Sears Tower, but because from almost any alley,
sentences.zh: 不是因为我能看到西尔斯大厦，而是因为从几乎任何一条小巷，

sentences.en: you can see these hefty, robust, wooden fire escapes climbing up the backs of two, three, and four-story brick apartment buildings.
sentences.zh: 你都能看到这些厚实、坚固的木制防火梯沿着两层、三层和四层砖砌公寓楼的背面向上延伸。

sentences.en: To call it a fire escape is almost a misnomer.
sentences.zh: 管它叫防火梯几乎有点名不副实。

sentences.en: They usually have a substantial landing on each floor, so they serve as a de facto porch,
sentences.zh: 它们通常在每层都有一个相当大的平台，因此它们实际上充当了门廊的角色，

sentences.en: a place to store things and hang out with a few friends, grill up some steaks,
sentences.zh: 一个存放东西、和几个朋友聚会、烤几块牛排的地方，

sentences.en: and meet the neighbors down in the alley below.
sentences.zh: 还能在下方的小巷里遇到邻居。

sentences.en: These wooden steps and porches started popping up in the early 1900s,
sentences.zh: 这些木制台阶和门廊在20世纪初开始涌现，

sentences.en: bolted onto buildings as a means of emergency escape,
sentences.zh: 作为紧急逃生的手段被用螺栓固定在建筑物上，

sentences.en: because of Chicago's very justified fear of fire.
sentences.zh: 因为芝加哥对火灾有着非常合理的恐惧。

sentences.en: They were utilitarian affairs that became so much more.
sentences.zh: 它们原本是实用主义的产物，却演变成了远超于此的存在。

sentences.en: It's safe to say that the vast majority of these were not designed by architects.
sentences.zh: 可以肯定地说，其中绝大多数都不是由建筑师设计的。

sentences.en: The one on the back of my apartment building in Logan Square was so structurally unsound,
sentences.zh: 我位于洛根广场的公寓楼背面的那个结构太不稳固了，

sentences.en: I don't think it was designed at all.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它根本就没被设计过。

sentences.en: This week, 99% Invisible Producers and friends of the show will be sharing more stories about vernacular architecture we love from our hometowns,
sentences.zh: 本周，99% Invisible的制作人们和节目的朋友们将分享更多关于我们热爱的家乡本土建筑的故事，

sentences.en: but with an emphasis on examples that may be a bit shaggier and have somewhat more functional origins.
sentences.zh: 但重点会放在那些可能显得有些粗糙且起源更具功能性的例子上。

sentences.en: They may not be the first things people call beautiful, but they're beautiful to us,
sentences.zh: 它们可能不是人们首先会称赞为美丽的事物，但对我们来说它们很美，

sentences.en: and they are essential parts of the places that are built.
sentences.zh: 并且它们是建成环境不可或缺的部分。

sentences.en: Up first is producer Emmett Fitzgerald.
sentences.zh: 首先登场的是制作人埃米特·菲茨杰拉德。

sentences.en: I grew up in central Vermont, in an old house on a hill.
sentences.zh: 我在佛蒙特州中部的一个小山丘上的老房子里长大。

sentences.en: It was built in the 1840s, a little farmhouse from a time when most people were farmers.
sentences.zh: 它建于19世纪40年代，是一座小型农舍，源于大多数人都是农民的那个时代。

sentences.en: Over the years, the house grew as my parents tacked on a room here and a room there,
sentences.zh: 多年来，随着我父母在这里加盖一个房间、那里加盖一个房间，房子不断扩大，

sentences.en: but in the kitchen, you can still see the original spruce beams with tiny curly Q tunnels carved by 19th century bugs.
sentences.zh: 但在厨房里，你仍然可以看到原始的云杉梁，上面刻有19世纪昆虫留下的微小卷曲隧道。

sentences.en: There are a lot of old farmhouses like mine along the dirt roads of Vermont.
sentences.zh: 佛蒙特州的泥土路旁有很多像我这样老旧的农舍。

sentences.en: Most of them were not designed by architects, but local carpenters who followed a few different traditional styles.
sentences.zh: 它们大多不是由建筑师设计的，而是由遵循几种不同传统风格的当地木匠建造的。

sentences.en: And like mine, most of these houses have grown and changed over the centuries, adapting to the needs of new generations.
sentences.zh: 和我的房子一样，这些房子大多在几个世纪中不断扩建和改变，以适应新一代的需求。

sentences.en: As a result, the farmhouses of Vermont don't have a single consistent look.
sentences.zh: 因此，佛蒙特州的农舍并没有单一连贯的外观。

sentences.en: But there is one bizarre architectural feature that you will find on lots of them.
sentences.zh: 但有一个奇怪的建筑特征，你在许多农舍上都能找到。

sentences.en: Windows that have been turned 45 degrees.
sentences.zh: 旋转了45度的窗户。

sentences.en: They're just like regular windows, but cockeyed, tilted,
sentences.zh: 它们就像普通的窗户，但却是歪的、倾斜的，

sentences.en: so that they run on a diagonal parallel with the roofline rather than straight up and down.
sentences.zh: 使其呈对角线排列，与屋顶线平行，而不是笔直地上下排列。

sentences.en: Growing up, I would see these windows all the time.
sentences.zh: 在成长过程中，我经常看到这些窗户。

sentences.en: Usually, you'd spot them on an old-looking farmhouse that might have an even older-looking barn lilting in the field out back.
sentences.zh: 通常，你会在一座看起来很古老的农舍上发现它们，其后方的田野里可能还伫立着一座看起来更古老的谷仓。

sentences.en: They always looked kind of otherworldly to me, like little glitches in the Matrix.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，它们总是显得有点超现实，就像黑客帝国里的一个小故障。

sentences.en: But to be honest, I didn't think that much about them.
sentences.zh: 但老实说，我并没有过多地思考它们。

sentences.en: They were all over Vermont, and I kind of assumed that they were all over other places, too.
sentences.zh: 它们遍布佛蒙特州，我一度以为它们在其他地方也随处可见。

sentences.en: It did not feel strange to me at all.
sentences.zh: 我一点也不觉得奇怪。

sentences.en: My friend Alice actually had one of these windows in her bedroom growing up.
sentences.zh: 我的朋友爱丽丝从小到大卧室里其实就有一扇这样的窗户。

sentences.en: And on a recent visit home from Chicago, she posted a few pictures of her childhood house to Instagram.
sentences.zh: 在她最近从芝加哥回家探亲时，她在Instagram上发布了几张她童年住所的照片。

sentences.en: Like, everybody here, to a T, was commenting, being like,
sentences.zh: 就像这里的每个人，无一例外地都在评论说：

sentences.en: that window is crazy.
sentences.zh: 那个窗户太疯狂了。

sentences.en: That's a crazy window.
sentences.zh: 那是个疯狂的窗户。

sentences.en: And I was like, is it?
sentences.zh: 而我的反应是：真的吗？

sentences.en: Like, in my mind, I was like, oh, I just, I grew up with this window.
sentences.zh: 就我心里而言，我会想，哦，我只是，我从小就和这扇窗户一起长大。

sentences.en: Like, I didn't realize it was crazy.
sentences.zh: 我之前并没有意识到这很疯狂。

sentences.en: It turns out that these crooked windows are found almost entirely in Vermont.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这些歪斜的窗户几乎只在佛蒙特州才能找到。

sentences.en: They go by a few different names, but are probably most commonly referred to as witch windows.
sentences.zh: 它们有几个不同的名字，但最常被提及的可能是“女巫窗”。

sentences.en: Legend has it the windows were tilted on a diagonal in order to prevent witches from flying into the house on their broomsticks.
sentences.zh: 传说这些窗户被倾斜成对角线，是为了防止女巫骑着扫帚飞进屋里。

sentences.en: A sort of architectural defense strategy.
sentences.zh: 这是一种建筑防御策略。

sentences.en: And I grew up thinking it's called a witch window because witches can't fly in it.
sentences.zh: 我从小就以为它被称为女巫窗是因为女巫无法从里面飞进来。

sentences.en: So I was safe from witches.
sentences.zh: 所以我免受女巫的侵害。

sentences.en: Why exactly a competent witch would be thwarted by a diagonal window is never quite explained.
sentences.zh: 至于为什么一个有能力的巫婆会被一扇对角窗阻挡，从来没有被完全解释过。

sentences.en: Because they can only fly straight, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我猜是因为她们只能直线飞行吧。

sentences.en: But there you go.
sentences.zh: 但事情就是这样。

sentences.en: Did that bring you a peace of mind?
sentences.zh: 这给你带来了心灵的平静吗？

sentences.en: Um, honestly, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，老实说，是的。

sentences.en: I grew up, I grew up a very fearful child of, um, paranormal things.
sentences.zh: 我长大时，我是一个对超自然事物非常恐惧的孩子。

sentences.en: And the, like, surroundings of my house were kind of spooky, too.
sentences.zh: 而且，我房子周围的环境也有点毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: Like, dark woods, and you don't know what's in there.
sentences.zh: 比如，阴暗树林，你根本不知道里面有什么。

sentences.en: So, like, yeah, really any sort of, uh, extra protection.
sentences.zh: 所以，真的，任何形式的额外保护都好。

sentences.en: Help.
sentences.zh: 帮助。

sentences.en: That's ridiculous to think about now, but it's true.
sentences.zh: 现在回想起来这很荒谬，但这是真的。

sentences.en: And like I said, these tilted windows, which you see all over Vermont, have a few different names.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，这些你在佛蒙特州各处都能看到的倾斜窗户有几个不同的名字。

sentences.en: Did you ever hear them referred to as coffin windows?
sentences.zh: 你听说过有人把它们叫做棺材窗吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Wait, why were they called coffin windows?
sentences.zh: 等等，为什么它们被称为棺材窗？

sentences.en: Okay, so this one makes even less sense in my opinion.
sentences.zh: 好吧，在我看来，这个说法更说不通。

sentences.en: But the story goes that they were called coffin windows because they enabled people to slide a coffin out of a second story window if someone happened to die upstairs.
sentences.zh: 但传说是这样的：它们被称为棺材窗，是因为如果有人不幸死在楼上，人们可以通过二楼的窗户把棺材滑出去。

sentences.en: I don't really understand how that would work physically or why you would bring the coffin upstairs rather than just bringing the body downstairs.
sentences.zh: 我实在搞不懂这在物理上是如何行得通的，或者为什么你要把棺材搬到楼上去，而不是直接把遗体抬下楼。

sentences.en: But the name has stuck around and added another layer of general spookiness to these windows.
sentences.zh: 但这个名字流传了下来，给这些窗户又添了一层普遍的诡异色彩。

sentences.en: Now, I headfully assumed that Alice's witch window or coffin window had been a part of the house's original construction or maybe some 19th century renovation.
sentences.zh: 现在，我原本理所当然地以为爱丽丝的女巫窗或棺材窗是房屋最初建造的一部分，或者是19世纪某种翻修的结果。

sentences.en: Their house was definitely old, from the same era as my parents.
sentences.zh: 他们的房子绝对很老，和我父母的房子属于同一时期。

sentences.en: And people aren't exactly out there installing new witch windows.
sentences.zh: 而且人们也不会无缘无故地跑去安装新的女巫窗。

sentences.en: At least, that's what I thought.
sentences.zh: 至少，我是这么认为的。

sentences.en: I actually asked my mom about it and she said that there used to be like a smaller window in there and then I was born and they wanted to have a window that a person could fit through just in case of emergencies.
sentences.zh: 我其实问过我妈妈这件事，她说那里以前有一个小一点的窗户，后来我出生了，他们想要一个万一遇到紧急情况人能钻得过去的窗户。

sentences.en: So she had that.
sentences.zh: 所以她就有了那个。

sentences.en: She had it put in.
sentences.zh: 她让人装了这个。

sentences.en: Which means that Alice's witch window was only a few decades old and was installed not to prevent witches from entering the house or to get coffins out,
sentences.zh: 这意味着爱丽丝的女巫窗只有几十年的历史，安装它不是为了防止女巫进入屋内，也不是为了运出棺材，

sentences.en: but to give little Alice an emergency exit in case of a fire.
sentences.zh: 而是为了给小爱丽丝在发生火灾时提供一个紧急出口。

sentences.en: Yeah, she put it in.
sentences.zh: 对，是她让人装的。

sentences.en: Oh, that's so interesting.
sentences.zh: 哦，太有趣了。

sentences.en: Maybe I should call your mom.
sentences.zh: 也许我应该给你妈妈打电话。

sentences.en: Yeah, you probably should.
sentences.zh: 对，你大概真该打一个。

sentences.en: I'm sorry, I'm not helpful at all.
sentences.zh: 对不起，我一点忙也帮不上。

sentences.en: Call my mom.
sentences.zh: 给我妈打电话。

sentences.en: Hey, Nancy.
sentences.zh: 嗨，南希。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: I'm good.
sentences.zh: 我很好。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你呢？

sentences.en: This is Nancy, mother of Alice.
sentences.zh: 这是南希，爱丽丝的母亲。

sentences.en: And as I learned in this conversation, the former architectural historian of the state of Vermont.
sentences.zh: 正如我在这次对话中了解到的，她曾任佛蒙特州的历史建筑学家。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I probably should have just called her firSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我一开始可能就该直接给她打电话。

sentences.en: So, Alice may have told you that I put in that window.
sentences.zh: 所以，爱丽丝可能跟你说过我装了那个窗户。

sentences.en: That's not original.
sentences.zh: 那不是原装的。

sentences.en: Nancy confirmed that she wanted to install the window to give Alice an escape route out the bedroom.
sentences.zh: 南希证实，她想安装这个窗户是为了给爱丽丝提供一条逃离卧室的路线。

sentences.en: But there was a problem.
sentences.zh: 但有个问题。

sentences.en: There just wasn't enough room.
sentences.zh: 空间实在不够。

sentences.en: Like a lot of old farmhouses in Vermont, the main part of the house is only one and a half stories tall.
sentences.zh: 就像佛蒙特州的许多老农舍一样，房子的主体部分只有一层半高。

sentences.en: And then there's a back wing that's even shorter.
sentences.zh: 然后后面还有一个更矮的翼楼。

sentences.en: And so Alice's second floor room was tucked under the slope of the gable roof.
sentences.zh: 所以爱丽丝的二楼房间刚好夹在斜面山墙屋顶下方。

sentences.en: And there just wasn't enough space for a regular vertical window.
sentences.zh: 根本没有足够的空间安装常规的垂直窗户。

sentences.en: But Nancy, being an expert in the historical architecture of Vermont, had an idea.
sentences.zh: 但是南希作为佛蒙特州历史建筑的专家，想到了一个主意。

sentences.en: I thought, well, I'll just use the old Vermont solution, which is to put in a window at an angle like that.
sentences.zh: 我想，好吧，我只要用老佛蒙特州的办法，就是以这样的角度安装一个窗户。

sentences.en: I asked the carpenters to put it in.
sentences.zh: 我请木匠把它装上了。

sentences.en: I thought I was a little bit crazy.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己当时有点疯狂。

sentences.en: Nancy says that this is the real reason these crooked windows exist in the first place.
sentences.zh: 南希说，这就是这些歪斜的窗户最初存在的真正原因。

sentences.en: It has nothing to do with witches or coffins.
sentences.zh: 这与女巫或棺材毫无关系。

sentences.en: It was just a clever architectural workaround.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个巧妙的建筑变通方案。

sentences.en: A simple, cheap solution for how to get a window into a space where one doesn't naturally fit.
sentences.zh: 一个简单、廉价的解决方案，用于解决如何在不自然契合的空间里塞进一扇窗户。

sentences.en: You could build a dormer, but that's expensive.
sentences.zh: 你可以建一个老虎窗，但那很贵。

sentences.en: And so at some point, some clever carpenter in Vermont had the idea to just salvage a regular window and turn it on an angle.
sentences.zh: 所以在某个时候，佛蒙特州某个聪明的木匠萌生了一个想法，干脆把一普通窗户拆下来，倾斜一个角度安装。

sentences.en: And then the idea just spread as a practical solution.
sentences.zh: 然后这个想法作为一种实用方案便传开了。

sentences.en: So, you know, it wasn't like it was a decorative feature of old houses.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，它并不是老房子的装饰性特征。

sentences.en: It was, I think, a very practical old Yankee solution to getting light and air into that room
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种非常实用的老杨基人解决方案，用来给那个房间引入光线和空气，

sentences.en: that otherwise doesn't have enough wall space to put a window to the outside.
sentences.zh: 否则该房间将没有足够的墙面空间来安装通往室外的窗户。

sentences.en: There's actually one more name that these windows sometimes go by.
sentences.zh: 实际上这些窗户有时还有一个名字。

sentences.en: Vermont windows.
sentences.zh: 佛蒙特窗。

sentences.en: It might not sound as cool as witch windows, but I think it's a pretty good name.
sentences.zh: 听起来可能没有女巫窗那么酷，但我认为这是一个相当不错的名字。

sentences.en: For an architectural feature that emerged from the collective genius of a bunch of anonymous Vermonters.
sentences.zh: 献给从一群无名佛蒙特人的集体智慧中涌现出来的建筑特征。

sentences.en: For our multi-part 500-episode milestone vernacular spectacular,
sentences.zh: 为了我们多部分组成的500期里程碑本土奇观特辑，

sentences.en: a lot of the staff have done stories that have focused on residential and personal architecture that's affected them.
sentences.zh: 许多工作人员都制作了聚焦于影响他们的住宅和个人建筑的故事。

sentences.en: But friend of the show and longtime contributor Katie Thornton is here to talk about the thing that she loves in her neighborhood in Minneapolis
sentences.zh: 但节目的朋友和长期撰稿人凯蒂·桑顿来到这里，要谈谈她在明尼阿波利斯街区喜爱的事物，

sentences.en: that is not residential at all.
sentences.zh: 那根本不是住宅。

sentences.en: It is industrial.
sentences.zh: 它是工业化的。

sentences.en: In fact, it is like aggressively industrial.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它具有强烈的工业感。

sentences.en: Yeah, aggressively industrial is the perfect description.
sentences.zh: 对，“强烈工业感”是完美的描述。

sentences.en: And certainly it is the architectural feature that dominates my neighborhood,
sentences.zh: 当然，这也是主导我所在街区的建筑特征，

sentences.en: stretches above homes, above trees.
sentences.zh: 高耸于房屋之上、树木之上。

sentences.en: And I'm talking about these huge concrete towers that we know as grain silos.
sentences.zh: 我说的就是这些我们称为谷仓的高大混凝土塔楼。

sentences.en: When I think a lot of people picture grain silos, they're like driving on a highway in the Midwest
sentences.zh: 当很多人脑海中浮现出谷仓时，他们会觉得就像在это中西部的高速公路上开车，

sentences.en: and they see one in the distance in this lone tower.
sentences.zh: 然后在远处看到一座孤零零的塔楼。

sentences.en: But this is not what is going on in your neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 但你所在的街区发生的并不是这样。

sentences.en: This is something a little bit more massive.
sentences.zh: 这是更具体量感的东西。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yes, so I live in Minneapolis.
sentences.zh: 是的，我住在明尼阿波利斯。

sentences.en: And so if you can imagine like one of those towers, but they usually are sort of domed.
sentences.zh: 如果你能想象其中一座塔，但它们通常顶部呈圆顶状。

sentences.en: If you see it out on a farm, chop off the dome and just bunch them all together like rows and rows, side by side.
sentences.zh: 如果你在农场看到它，砍掉圆顶，然后把它们像一排排一样紧紧挤在一起，并排而立。

sentences.en: They're these sort of massive concrete compounds that just are used to store tons and tons of grain
sentences.zh: 它们是那种巨大的混凝土建筑，专门用来储存成吨成吨的谷物

sentences.en: and stretching for blocks and blocks and blocks.
sentences.zh: 而且绵延了好几个街区。

sentences.en: And you currently live under the shadow of one.
sentences.zh: 你现在就住在其中一座的阴影下。

sentences.en: What is that like?
sentences.zh: 那是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Yeah, I love it.
sentences.zh: 对，我很喜欢。

sentences.en: I've lived here for a number of years now.
sentences.zh: 我在这里已经住了好几年了。

sentences.en: It means that my garden is always a little bit pitiful.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我的花园总是有点凄凉。

sentences.en: Like I don't I'm robbed of some like pretty precious hours of sunlight every day, but it is still very much worth it.
sentences.zh: 就像我每天都被剥夺了一些非常宝贵的阳光，但它仍然非常值得。

sentences.en: And the silos is like they're kind of funny.
sentences.zh: 而且这些筒仓挺有意思的。

sentences.en: You know, they like almost to apologize for like, oh, sorry, your garden sucks.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它们几乎就像是在道歉，哦，抱歉，你的花园太糟糕了。

sentences.en: It's like here we spilled a bunch of grain all over the train tracks that are adjacent to the silos.
sentences.zh: 就像是我们把一堆谷物洒在了紧挨着筒仓的铁轨上。

sentences.en: So you have this like annoyingly idyllic surplus of bunnies and other little critters.
sentences.zh: 所以你就会拥有这种烦人的、田园牧歌般的过剩兔子和其他小动物。

sentences.en: And then in turn, that means there's red-tailed hawks and falcons who live up in the crevices and the cracks of the silos.
sentences.zh: 反过来，这就意味着红尾鹰和猎鹰会住在筒仓的缝隙里。

sentences.en: And they're just eating like very well.
sentences.zh: 它们吃得相当好。

sentences.en: You know, I think I picture you living near an abandoned silo for some reason.
sentences.zh: 你知道，不知为什么，我脑海中浮现出你住在废弃筒仓附近的画面。

sentences.en: And there are tons of abandoned ones, but yours is full of grain.
sentences.zh: 确实有大量的废弃筒仓，但你的里面装满了谷物。

sentences.en: That's actually really cool.
sentences.zh: 这其实真的很酷。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So why are there so many grain silos in Minneapolis?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么明尼阿波利斯会有这么多粮仓呢？

sentences.en: Like what was going on when their boom happened?
sentences.zh: 当它们繁荣发展时，究竟发生了什么？

sentences.en: I think that's really gets to like one of the reasons why I like the silos is that it's this big visual reminder of why the city grew in the first place.
sentences.zh: 我想这真正触及了我喜欢筒仓的原因之一，因为它是这座城市最初为何发展壮大的巨大视觉提醒。

sentences.en: The area has been home to indigenous people for millennia since long before, long before white colonists settled here.
sentences.zh: 几千年来，早在白人殖民者在这里定居之前很久，这个地区就是原住民的家园。

sentences.en: But starting in the 1800s, this burgeoning city of Minneapolis was built on the Mississippi River,
sentences.zh: 但从 19 世纪开始，这座蓬勃发展的明尼阿波利斯市建立在密西西比河畔，

sentences.en: on the area where there's the only sort of significant natural waterfall on the entirety of the Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 位于整个密西西比河唯一一处重要的天然瀑布所在地。

sentences.en: And eventually they were able to use the power of that waterfall to power flour mills where they ground up wheat, which was grown in the area nearby.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们能够利用这处瀑布的水力来驱动面粉厂，在那里磨碎附近种植的小麦。

sentences.en: So milling became the city's biggest industry really quickly.
sentences.zh: 因此，面粉加工很快成为该市最大的产业。

sentences.en: And as the railroads were built,
sentences.zh: 随着铁路的修建，

sentences.en: more and more unprocessed grain could come in from farms from throughout the region and get processed by the mills in the city and then be stored in silos like the one near me or shipped down the river or shipped out by train.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的未加工谷物从全地区的农场运来，由城里的面粉厂加工，然后储存在像我附近这样的筒仓里，或者顺流而下运走，或通过火车运出。

sentences.en: So there's this sort of interconnected man-made and natural systems that all sort of converge and coincide right here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有这种相互交织的人造和自然系统，它们都在这里汇聚和重合。

sentences.en: And then you add to it that these crops are seasonal.
sentences.zh: 然后你再加上这些农作物是季节性的。

sentences.en: So you get a whole bunch at once and you have to deal with it.
sentences.zh: 所以你一次性能得到一大堆，你必须处理它们。

sentences.en: So you have to find a way to store it somehow.
sentences.zh: 因此你必须想办法把它们储存起来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so in order to sort of solve this problem of storing grain, like farmers for a long, long time would just store it on their property.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了解决储存谷物的问题，很长一段时间以来，农民们只会把它储存在自己的地产上。

sentences.en: For the most part, since the 1800s, the buildings that held grain were wooden and square, like many buildings, as you may be aware, are built.
sentences.zh: 在大多数情况下，自 19 世纪以来，存放谷物的建筑都是木质和方形的，就像你可能知道的许多建筑一样。

sentences.en: But there was sort of this problem, which is that like when they were filled, there would be these air pockets in the corners.
sentences.zh: 但当时存在这样一个问题，就是当它们被填满时，角落里会有气囊。

sentences.en: They wouldn't just fill out, you know, like a cat fills out every corner of a cardboard box.
sentences.zh: 它们不会像猫填满纸箱的每一个角落那样填满。

sentences.en: You know, it would just like not reach into the corners.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它就是伸不到角落里。

sentences.en: And then this little bit of air would lead to all of this grain rot.
sentences.zh: 然后这点空气就会导致所有这些谷物腐烂。

sentences.en: And so that was sort of a problem for farmers.
sentences.zh: 所以这算是农民的一个问题。

sentences.en: It was a problem for grain merchants.
sentences.zh: 这对谷物商人来说是个问题。

sentences.en: And also wooden silos were just super prone to catching on fire.
sentences.zh: 而且木制筒仓也非常容易着火。

sentences.en: So this grain merchant, Frank Peavy, sick of losing his grain to rot, didn't want to pay these high fire insurance premiuMs.
sentences.zh: 所以这位谷物商人弗兰克·皮维（Frank Peavy），厌倦了谷物腐烂造成的损失，也不想支付高昂的火灾保险费。

sentences.en: And so he wanted to figure out how to store the grain in a different way.
sentences.zh: 因此他想弄清楚如何用不同的方式来储存谷物。

sentences.en: And so he brought along this contractor named Charles Hagelin, and they wanted to try something different.
sentences.zh: 于是他找来了一位名叫查尔斯·哈格林（Charles Hagelin）的承包商，他们想尝试一些不同的东西。

sentences.en: Well, wood is flammable.
sentences.zh: 好吧，木头是易燃的。

sentences.en: Let's try concrete, which hadn't been done before.
sentences.zh: 让我们试试混凝土吧，以前还没人这么做过。

sentences.en: And also, you know, this whole square building thing, it isn't really working.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这种方形建筑的套路真的行不通。

sentences.en: The corners are the problem.
sentences.zh: 角落才是问题所在。

sentences.en: Let's just make it round.
sentences.zh: 我们把它做成圆的吧。

sentences.en: And so in the late 1800s, they decided to build up a prototype of a cylindrical concrete grain silo to sort of prove that their idea could work.
sentences.zh: 因此在 19 世纪末，他们决定建造一个圆柱形混凝土粮仓的原型，以证明他们的想法是可行的。

sentences.en: You know, the typology of a cylinder makes so much sense.
sentences.zh: 你知道，圆柱体的类型学是如此合理。

sentences.en: It's almost surprising that they didn't come up with this sooner.
sentences.zh: 他们没有早点想到这一点，几乎让人感到意外。

sentences.en: But I think you're right.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你是对的。

sentences.en: It did surprise me it didn't come up sooner.
sentences.zh: 它没有早点出现确实让我感到意外。

sentences.en: And honestly, what surprised me even more is that, like, even when they came up with this idea at the tail end of the 1800s, everyone was like, terrible idea.
sentences.zh: 老实说，更让我感到意外的是，即使他们在 19 世纪末尾想出这个主意时，每个人都觉得：这主意太糟了。

sentences.en: Going to be an absolute flop.
sentences.zh: 绝对会彻底砸锅。

sentences.en: What are you thinking?
sentences.zh: 你在想什么呢？

sentences.en: Like, they started to build this structure.
sentences.zh: 就像，他们开始建造这个结构。

sentences.en: And before they could even finish the prototype, people had dubbed it Peavy's Folly, which is just like a very cruel thing to do.
sentences.zh: 甚至在原型建完之前，人们就已经把它称为“皮维的傻事”（Peavy's Folly），这简直是一件非常残酷的事情。

sentences.en: It's not like it had failed.
sentences.zh: 这又不是说它失败了。

sentences.en: He just literally wasn't done.
sentences.zh: 他只是字面意义上还没建完。

sentences.en: So people just were like, this is a stupid idea.
sentences.zh: 所以人们只是觉得，这是个愚蠢的主意。

sentences.en: This is never going to work.
sentences.zh: 这永远不会成功。

sentences.en: And they thought that either the cement wouldn't be strong enough,
sentences.zh: 他们认为要么是水泥不够坚固，

sentences.en: like the sheer volume of the grain that was pushing out on the silo from the inside would just be enough to force it to crack or burst, which, you know, I guess valid concern.
sentences.zh: 比如从内部向外推挤筒仓的庞大谷物体积，就足以迫使其开裂或爆裂，你知道的，我想这倒是个合理的担忧。

sentences.en: I would probably have similar concerns about wood.
sentences.zh: 我对木头可能也会有类似的担忧。

sentences.en: Also, they thought that, well, this airtight tower is going to create a vacuum.
sentences.zh: 此外，他们认为，这个气密塔会产生真空。

sentences.en: And so when you open a door at the bottom and let the grain spill out, which is how you get the grain out, it's just going to implode.
sentences.zh: 所以当你打开底部的门让谷物涌出（这是你取出谷物的方式）时，它会内爆。

sentences.en: It's just going to collapse.
sentences.zh: 它会直接坍塌。

sentences.en: People thought it was a terrible idea.
sentences.zh: 人们认为这是个糟糕的主意。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So they build their prototype and people are skeptical.
sentences.zh: 所以他们建造了原型，而人们持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: What happens next?
sentences.zh: 接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, as you can probably imagine, based on how grain silos look today, PV proved to them all wrong.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如你大概能想象的那样，根据今天粮仓的外表，皮维证明了他们所有人都错了。

sentences.en: There was a day set where they were going to fill their demonstration piece and hundreds of people gathered to like watch this drama because this is like the big news of the day.
sentences.zh: 有一天，他们设定了要填满演示样件的日子，数百人聚集在一起观看这场大戏，因为这是当天的特大新闻。

sentences.en: The silo is going to explode.
sentences.zh: 筒仓要爆炸了。

sentences.en: It's going to collapse.
sentences.zh: 它要坍塌了。

sentences.en: It's going to whatever.
sentences.zh: 它要发生这样那样的事了。

sentences.en: So they cordoned people off from this supposed blast zone.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们将人群从这个所谓的爆炸区拉起警戒线隔离开来。

sentences.en: It was this whole to-do.
sentences.zh: 这搞得兴师动众的。

sentences.en: The New York Times even sent a reporter out.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》甚至派了一名记者过来。

sentences.en: And then what are you going to report on?
sentences.zh: 然后你还要报道什么呢？

sentences.en: It went off without a hitch.
sentences.zh: 它进展得非常顺利。

sentences.en: And then they began to crop up everywhere.
sentences.zh: 然后它们开始到处涌现。

sentences.en: Everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处都是。

sentences.en: So the silos near me were sort of built shortly after this very first concrete cylindrical grain silo.
sentences.zh: 所以我附近的筒仓就是在第一个混凝土圆柱形粮仓建成后不久建造的。

sentences.en: And, you know, they were really built to laSt.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，它们真的是为了持久而建造的。

sentences.en: Like they were not built with any consideration for people's aesthetic desires necessarily.
sentences.zh: 就像它们建造时根本没有考虑人们的审美需求一样。

sentences.en: But they were definitely built to last, hence still living behind them.
sentences.zh: 但它们绝对是为了持久而建的，因此至今仍有人住在它们后面。

sentences.en: But as you mentioned, milling is no longer the primary source of industrial income when it comes to Minneapolis.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所提到的，就明尼阿波利斯而言，面粉加工已不再是工业收入的主要来源。

sentences.en: So what happens when you have this robust piece of industrial infrastructure that can last, you know, 110 years when there is no longer grain to be milled?
sentences.zh: 所以，当你拥有这样一个能够持续 110 年之久的坚固工业基础设施，而又不再有需要加工的谷物时，会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: So, you know, for those silos that are still operational, they're one of the rare pieces of industrial design that still operates as intended, like 100 plus years later,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，对于那些仍在运营的筒仓，它们是罕见的仍按预期运行的工业设计之一，历经 100 多年依然如此，

sentences.en: which is pretty darn remarkable.
sentences.zh: 这相当了不起。

sentences.en: But for those that aren't operational, they've proven really difficult to repurpose.
sentences.zh: 但对于那些没有运营的筒仓，事实证明要重新规划它们的用途非常困难。

sentences.en: I love to see the silos that have been repurposed across the country.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴看到全国各地被重新改造利用的筒仓。

sentences.en: Some have been retrofitted as hotels.
sentences.zh: 有些被改造成了酒店。

sentences.en: There are brewery facilities.
sentences.zh: 有啤酒厂设施。

sentences.en: There's some condos.
sentences.zh: 有一些是公寓。

sentences.en: There's even some condos here in Minneapolis.
sentences.zh: 明尼阿波利斯这里甚至还有一些公寓。

sentences.en: You don't even recognize it.
sentences.zh: 你甚至认不出来。

sentences.en: When you walk past, it's like I biked past this one building that was a retrofitted grain silo that is now condos for years and years of my childhood.
sentences.zh: 当你走过时，就像我童年时骑车经过一栋改造后的粮仓建筑，它现在已经是公寓，一过就是好多年。

sentences.en: And it took me until this year, this story, to be like, oh, those were silos.
sentences.zh: 直到今年，通过这个故事，我才恍然大悟：哦，原来那些是筒仓。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 噢，哇。

sentences.en: You know, I've heard it said on this show, good design is 99% invisible.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我在这个节目里听人说过，好的设计是 99% 隐形的。

sentences.en: And I could not agree more.
sentences.zh: 我对此不能同意更多。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I just kind of happen to live at one of those junctures where it's just unavoidably visible.
sentences.zh: 但我刚好住在那些无法避免地显而易见的交汇点之一。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's sort of this like relay station in this big urban design where like our infrastructure has to come up for air.
sentences.zh: 它有点像这种宏大城市设计中的中继站，我们的基础设施必须在这里透透气。

sentences.en: It has to be seen.
sentences.zh: 它必须被看到。

sentences.en: It has to be seen at what makes a city tick or even just what used to make a city tick.
sentences.zh: 它必须让人看到是什么让一座城市运转，或者甚至是曾经是什么让一座城市运转。

sentences.en: Well, thank you so much for talking with us and sharing your love of grain silos.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢你与我们交谈并分享你对粮仓的热爱。

sentences.en: Thanks, Roman.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，罗曼。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me on.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: And congratulations on a 500 and 501st episode.
sentences.zh: 祝贺迎来第 500 和 501 期节目。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: I'm amazed myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己也很吃惊。

sentences.en: The global appetite for talking about grain silos and maintenance hold covers was stronger than I thought.
sentences.zh: 人们对谈论粮仓和井盖的全球热情比我想象的还要高涨。

sentences.en: Well, I'm honored to be a small part of it.
sentences.zh: 能成为其中的一小部分，我感到很荣幸。

sentences.en: We're going to shout at the sky with Jason DeLeon after this.
sentences.zh: 接下来我们将与杰森·德莱昂（Jason DeLeon）一起向天空呐喊。

sentences.en: Here's producer Jason DeLeon.
sentences.zh: 这是制作人杰森·德莱昂。

sentences.en: A few weeks back, my dad texted me this video that he shot on his phone.
sentences.zh: 几周前，我爸爸给我发了这段他用手机拍的视频。

sentences.en: That's what we get after 93 degrees.
sentences.zh: 气温高达 93 度，这就是我们的下场。

sentences.en: Después de 93 grados hoy.
sentences.zh: 今天的气温高达 93 度。

sentences.en: Another five o'clock summer storm is ripping through the east side of Orlando.
sentences.zh: 另一场五点钟的夏日风暴正肆虐奥兰多东区。

sentences.en: And my dad, well, he opened up a bottle of wine a bit early.
sentences.zh: 至于我爸，嗯，他稍微有点早地打开了一瓶酒。

sentences.en: I can hear it in his voice.
sentences.zh: 我从他的声音里能听得出来。

sentences.en: Two octaves up, yelling commands at the wind.
sentences.zh: 音高高了两个八度，正对着风大喊大叫地下达指令。

sentences.en: Whoa, whoa, slow down.
sentences.zh: 噢，噢，慢点。

sentences.en: Slow down.
sentences.zh: 慢点。

sentences.en: My goodness.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: I love when my dad sends me these weather updates, partly because they're incredible to watch.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢我爸发给我这些天气更新，部分原因是因为它们看起来太不可思议了。

sentences.en: Rain coming down like an open faucet, palm trees bending till they nearly break, but also partly because of where he is when he films these videos.
sentences.zh: 雨下得像开着的龙头，棕榈树弯曲得几乎要折断，但部分原因也是因为他拍摄这些视频时所处的位置。

sentences.en: He's almost always out back on what most people might call a screened-in porch.
sentences.zh: 他几乎总是在大多数人所谓的带纱窗的门廊后面的露台上。

sentences.en: But down in Florida, we take this screened-in porch to a whole new level.
sentences.zh: 但在佛罗里达州，我们将这种带纱窗的门廊提升到了一个全新的水平。

sentences.en: We have lanai's.
sentences.zh: 我们有露台（lanai）。

sentences.en: How did I call you, mom?
sentences.zh: 妈妈，我是怎么称呼你的？

sentences.en: I grew up around lanai's, bouncing from one to the next the way some kids jump from backyard to backyard or basement to basement.
sentences.zh: 我在露台（lanai）周围长大，从一个跳到另一个，就像有些孩子从一个后院跳到另一个后院，或者从一个地下室跳到另一个地下室一样。

sentences.en: That's because in Florida, especially in the newly developed areas, you can find lanai's everywhere.
sentences.zh: 那是因为在佛罗里达州，特别是在新开发的地区，你到处都能找到露台（lanai）。

sentences.en: Fly into the Orlando International Airport, and as you descend, yes, you'll see some of the worst urban sprawl America has to offer, but also lanai's.
sentences.zh: 飞往奥兰多国际机场，当你下降时，是的，你会看到美国所能提供的最糟糕的城市扩张，但也能看到露台（lanai）。

sentences.en: This space that's both inside and outside, where you can invite the elements into your home or keep nature at bay.
sentences.zh: 这个空间既在室内又在室外，你可以在这里把大自然元素请进家门，或者将大自然阻挡在外。

sentences.en: And maybe you've never come across one yourself, or only heard the word thrown around on an episode of Golden Girls.
sentences.zh: 也许你从未亲自遇到过，或者只在《黄金女郎》（Golden Girls）的一集里听到过这个词。

sentences.en: Is Dorothy around?
sentences.zh: 多萝西在吗？

sentences.en: She's out on the lanai.
sentences.zh: 她在露台上。

sentences.en: I suppose you're wondering why a man likes sunny balls.
sentences.zh: 我想你在纳闷为什么一个男人喜欢阳光球。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 耶，耶，耶，耶。

sentences.en: On the lanai.
sentences.zh: 在露台上。

sentences.en: But to me, and apparently to Blanche, the Florida lanai is quintessential to the whole Sunshine State experience.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，显然对布兰奇（Blanche）来说，佛罗里达的露台（lanai）是整个阳光之州体验的核心。

sentences.en: If you've never seen a Florida lanai, you might think it sounds kind of fancy or exotic, but really, the structure's simple.
sentences.zh: 如果你从未见过佛罗里达的露台（lanai），你可能会觉得它听起来有点高级或异国情调，但实际上，这个结构很简单。

sentences.en: It's an outdoor living space that's typically box-shaped and has this mesh screen enclosure separating the home from the yard.
sentences.zh: 这是一个户外的起居空间，通常呈盒状，并有一个网状的纱窗围栏将房屋与院子隔开。

sentences.en: On the outside, it sort of looks like a baseball batting cage, but on the inside, it gives off this vibe of a living room wearing boat shoes.
sentences.zh: 从外面看，它有点像棒球击球笼，但在里面，它散发着一种穿着船鞋的客厅的氛围。

sentences.en: Aesthetics aside, the lanai is a solution to some common Florida probleMs.
sentences.zh: 抛开美学不谈，游廊（lanai）其实是解决佛罗里达一些常见问题的方法。

sentences.en: For instance, that screen enclosure?
sentences.zh: 比如说，那个纱窗围栏？

sentences.en: In some of the newer constructions from the housing boom of the early 2000s, you'll see lanai's with in-ground pools built inside the screen enclosure.
sentences.zh: 在2000年代初住房热潮的一些较新的建筑中，你会看到游廊里面建有内置游泳池，并且被包裹在纱窗围栏里。

sentences.en: This helps keep your pool from becoming just another Florida swamp.
sentences.zh: 这有助于防止你的泳池变成另一个佛罗里达沼泽。

sentences.en: And if you have a little bit more change in your pocket, you'll see lanai's that are fully souped up,
sentences.zh: 如果你手头更宽裕一点，你会看到设施完全升级的游廊，

sentences.en: equipped with outdoor kitchens and enough space to host gigantic dinner parties.
sentences.zh: 配备了户外厨房，并且有足够的空间来举办盛大的晚宴。

sentences.en: So, depending on your tax bracket, it can be a modest chair or two with a table in the back corner of your home or a Miami Vice-style extravaganza.
sentences.zh: 所以，根据你的纳税等级，它可能是你家后角落里放着一张桌子的朴素的一两把椅子，也可能是迈阿密风云风格的奢华大空间。

sentences.en: When I think of lanai, I think of my parents' Florida lanai.
sentences.zh: 当我想到游廊时，我想到了我父母在佛罗里达的游廊。

sentences.en: But for Dean Sakamoto, who's studied the history of the structure, he takes it back to its indigenous roots.
sentences.zh: 但对于研究这种建筑历史的迪恩·萨卡莫托（Dean Sakamoto）来说，他将其追溯到它的本土根源。

sentences.en: The lanai, as you saw, as you know, it's a native Hawaiian word.
sentences.zh: 正如你所看到的，如你所知，游廊（lanai）是一个夏威夷本土词汇。

sentences.en: It's really a basic, a primal structure, like a four-posted structure just with enough cover to keep the sun out.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是一个基础的、原始的结构，就像一个四根柱子的结构，只有足够的遮盖来挡住阳光。

sentences.en: Dean co-authored a book about one of Hawaii's most renowned architects, Vladimir Osipov.
sentences.zh: 迪恩与人合著了一本关于夏威夷最著名建筑师之一弗拉基米尔·奥西波夫（Vladimir Osipov）的书。

sentences.en: He says Osipov helped modernize and popularize the lanai throughout the mid-20th century.
sentences.zh: 他说，在20世纪中期，奥西波夫帮助推动了游廊的现代化并使其广受欢迎。

sentences.en: Mr. Osipov, although he's Russian by birth, he grew up in Japan.
sentences.zh: 奥西波夫先生虽然出生于俄罗斯，但他在日本长大。

sentences.en: And so he grew up in a Japanese-style home.
sentences.zh: 因此他是在日式住宅中长大的。

sentences.en: And if you look at Japanese architecture, the domestic Japanese house, there's a space called the engawa.
sentences.zh: 如果你看一下日本建筑，也就是日本的住宅，会发现有一个叫做缘侧（engawa）的空间。

sentences.en: The engawa is a sort of precursor to the lanai.
sentences.zh: 缘侧可以说是游廊的前身。

sentences.en: It's a narrow, covered hallway built in between the interior rooms of an old Japanese home and the garden.
sentences.zh: 它是日本老房子的室内房间与花园之间修建的一个狭窄的、有屋顶的走廊。

sentences.en: Left open, the engawa allows for natural light in the air to circulate.
sentences.zh: 保持开放的话，缘侧可以让自然光和空气流通。

sentences.en: The space has this incentive to coexist with nature, not resist it.
sentences.zh: 这个空间有着与自然共存、而不是抗拒自然的意图。

sentences.en: An idea Osipov used for his lanais on the islands.
sentences.zh: 奥西波夫将这个理念运用到了他在岛屿上设计的游廊中。

sentences.en: When he came to Hawaii, he realized that the Japanese house is perhaps more appropriate in Hawaii than Japan because of the climate.
sentences.zh: 当他来到夏威夷时，他意识到由于气候原因，日式住宅在夏威夷可能比在日本更合适。

sentences.en: You know, in Japan, it gets cold.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在日本，天气很冷。

sentences.en: Osipov designed hundreds of luxury homes in Hawaii.
sentences.zh: 奥西波夫在夏威夷设计了数百栋豪华住宅。

sentences.en: In almost all of them, the lanai is the crown jewel of the house, his canvas to showcase a new style of tropical modernism.
sentences.zh: 在几乎所有的住宅中，游廊都是房子的皇冠明珠，是他展示热带现代主义新风格的画布。

sentences.en: Osipov made his imprint on Hawaiian architecture throughout the 1950s and 60s.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪50年代和60年代，奥西波夫在夏威夷建筑界留下了他的印记。

sentences.en: During that time, Hawaii itself was changing, turning from an American territory with an economy based on agriculture to a state with a booming tourism industry.
sentences.zh: 在那期间，夏威夷本身也在发生变化，从一个以农业为基础经济的美属领地转变为一个旅游业蓬勃发展的州。

sentences.en: And with that tourism came large-scale developments.
sentences.zh: 随着旅游业的发展，大规模的开发也随之而来。

sentences.en: Famously, at a press conference, Osipov announced the, quote, war on ugliness when he saw cheap, cookie-cutter-style housing creeping onto the shores of Honolulu.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，在一次新闻发布会上，奥西波夫宣布了所谓的“丑陋之战”，因为他看到廉价的、千篇一律的住宅开始蔓延到檀香山的海岸。

sentences.en: For locals trying to attract mainland travelers, the lanai was a defining feature of the state's architectural identity.
sentences.zh: 对于试图吸引美国大陆游客的当地人来说，游廊是该州建筑特色的一個决定性特征。

sentences.en: It was unique, a space that embodied the virtues of island life.
sentences.zh: 它是独一无二的，是一个体现岛屿生活优点的空间。

sentences.en: Around the same time of Hawaii's transformation, mentions of a tropical room borrowed from Pacific Islanders appeared in newspapers around Florida.
sentences.zh: 大约在夏威夷转型时期的同时，佛罗里达州各地的报纸上开始出现借用自太平洋岛民的热带房间的提及。

sentences.en: One article from 1964 raves about the lanai.
sentences.zh: 1964年的一篇文章对游廊赞不绝口。

sentences.en: It says it's the most exciting concept in indoor-outdoor living ever presented to the Central Florida new homebuyer.
sentences.zh: 文章称它是向佛罗里达州中部新购房者展示的关于室内外生活的最令人兴奋的概念。

sentences.en: Another highlights it as a way to, quote, plan for happy living.
sentences.zh: 另一篇文章强调它是“规划快乐生活”的一种方式。

sentences.en: You can see how the idea is exciting and new, but you can also see how it differs from an Osipov lanai.
sentences.zh: 你可以看出这个想法是多么令人兴奋和新颖，但你也能看出它与奥西波夫式的游廊有何不同。

sentences.en: While Osipov's lanai's were highbrow, custom-made and built to take into account the cooling trade winds and stormy Kona winds of Hawaii,
sentences.zh: 虽然奥西波夫的游廊是高雅的、定制的，并且在建造时考虑了夏威夷凉爽的信风和多风暴的科纳风，

sentences.en: the Florida lanai was a completely different species, more rudimentary and undefined.
sentences.zh: 但佛罗里达的游廊完全是另一个物种，更加初级且不那么明确。

sentences.en: Much like Hawaii, Florida was going through its own transformation with its own housing boom.
sentences.zh: 就像夏威夷一样，佛罗里达州也正在经历自身的转型和房屋建设热潮。

sentences.en: In some of the floor plans from the 60s and 70s, you can feel the developer's hand of excitement trying to see just where a lanai can be squeezed in.
sentences.zh: 在60年代和70年代的一些平面图中，你能感受到开发商那种兴奋的手笔，正试图看看究竟在哪里可以硬塞进一个游廊。

sentences.en: Today, builders have taken it a step further, more or less standardizing the placement and look of a lanai so that each one is nearly indistinguishable from the next.
sentences.zh: 如今，建筑商将这一概念推进了一步，或多或少地将游廊的位置和外观标准化，以至于每一个游廊都与下一个几乎没有区别。

sentences.en: And the homes are packed together so tightly that the lanai has become a way to effectively offer an outdoor space without giving the home an actual yard.
sentences.zh: 而且房屋建得如此密集，以至于游廊已经成为一种有效提供户外空间而又不给房屋留出实际院子的方式。

sentences.en: If Osipov's war on ugliness and cookie-cutter housing started in Hawaii, it ended in defeat in Orlando.
sentences.zh: 如果奥西波夫针对丑陋和千篇一律住宅的战争始于夏威夷，那么它最终在奥兰多以失败告终。

sentences.en: But still, I can't quite shake this fondness for this strange Floridian architectural creature.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，我还是无法摆脱对这种奇怪的佛罗里达建筑生物的喜爱。

sentences.en: Objectively, the typical Florida lanai is kind of bulky and ugly and batting cagey,
sentences.zh: 客观地说，典型的佛罗里达游廊有点笨重、难看，还带有棒球笼的风格，

sentences.en: but I have this very don't-make-fun-of-my-ugly-puppy feeling about them.
sentences.zh: 但我对它们有一种“不准嘲笑我的丑小狗”的感觉。

sentences.en: In Florida, a place where most people move to unabashedly have more, the lanai feels like the most appropriate place to indulge in that excess.
sentences.zh: 在佛罗里达这个大多数人搬来是为了毫无顾忌地拥有更多的地方，游廊感觉就像是纵情享受这种过度最合适的地方。

sentences.en: And in my family, there's a spirit to the space.
sentences.zh: 而在我的家庭里，这个空间有一种精神。

sentences.en: It's where we gather at the end of a long day to collectively shake ourselves loose.
sentences.zh: 这是我们在漫长一天结束时聚在一起，集体放松身心的地方。

sentences.en: It's where we sit around for hours on end playing dominoes for dollars.
sentences.zh: 这是我们连续坐上几个小时打多米诺骨牌赢美元的地方。

sentences.en: Listening to bachata and merengue while others sit around and tell stories about people long gone drinking Coronas and Mama Juana until we're fresh out.
sentences.zh: 听着巴查塔和梅伦格音乐，而其他人则坐在一起讲述那些早已离去的人的故事，喝着科罗娜和玛玛胡安娜啤酒，直到我们把酒喝个精光。

sentences.en: Even now when I go home to visit, the long talks with my mom where I finally get to sit her down and ask her,
sentences.zh: 即使是现在，当我回家探亲时，与妈妈进行的长谈，我终于能让她坐下来问她，

sentences.en: Hey, how are you?
sentences.zh: 嘿，你最近怎么样？

sentences.en: And tell my dad that I'm doing okay.
sentences.zh: 并告诉爸爸我过得挺好的。

sentences.en: That I'm figuring it out.
sentences.zh: 告诉他我正在摸索前行。

sentences.en: That I'm excited about this little life I'm starting.
sentences.zh: 告诉他我对开始的这种小生活感到兴奋。

sentences.en: Those talks do not happen at the dinner table.
sentences.zh: 那些谈话不是在餐桌旁进行的。

sentences.en: They happen in the lanai.
sentences.zh: 它们是在游廊里进行的。

sentences.en: And yes, even though I only get down to visit a few times a year, I still love to watch a storm roll in.
sentences.zh: 是的，尽管我一年只回去探亲几次，但我依然喜欢看风暴卷集而来的情景。

sentences.en: To feel the temperature in the air drop as the rain hits the hot pavement.
sentences.zh: 感受雨水拍打在炽热路面上时空气中温度的下降。

sentences.en: Counting the time between the cracks of thunder and streaks of lightning.
sentences.zh: 数着雷声炸裂和闪电划过之间的间隔时间。

sentences.en: Wondering if that last one touched the ground.
sentences.zh: 琢磨着最后那一闪是不是击中了地面。

sentences.en: And probably my favorite part of all,
sentences.zh: 可能也是我最喜欢的部分，

sentences.en: It's still an eye where I get to sit and watch as the clouds clear and give way again to that beautiful grapefruit-colored Florida sky.
sentences.zh: 那仍旧是一个我可以坐着看乌云散去，再次呈现出那种美丽的葡萄柚色佛罗里达天空的游廊。

sentences.en: We have one more episode in this series celebrating 500 episodes next week.
sentences.zh: 下周我们将推出本系列的最后一集，庆祝我们的第500集。

sentences.en: If you could continue to spread the word and encourage people to listen to this or any episode of 99% Invisible or write a review, I'd be so grateful.
sentences.zh: 如果你能继续广为宣传，鼓励人们收听这一集或《99%无形》的任何一集，或者写一篇评论，我将不胜感激。
